This appeal is by the claimants questioning the quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.1546/2016.
The respondent No.2/Insurance company admits its liability and therefore, the appeal is purely on quantum.

sentences.text: 2 2. The appellants have filed a claim petition in MVC.No.1546/2016 for having lost one Prakash in a road traffic accident dated 11.08.2016.
The claimants are parents, widow and two minor daughters.

The claimants contended that deceased was working as a Bus Conductor in NWKRTC, Hubli and was drawing a salary of Rs.25,000/- along with incentive amounting to Rs.5,000/- and also had an agricultural income of Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
3.

The Tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and while determining compensation under the head loss of dependency, the Tribunal strangely proceeded NC: 2024:KHC-K:9520 to deduct 10% towards income tax having recorded a finding that deceased was drawing salary of Rs.20,218/-.
The accident is of the year 2016 and the income tax rates for the assessment year 2016-17 clearly reveals that upto Rs.2,50,000/-, there is complete exemption.
His salary is taxable in excess of Rs.2,50,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.36,84,730/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.
The Tribunal in all has awarded Rs.37,54,730/-.
4. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants and learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance company.
Perused the records.
5. The deceased was employed as a Bus Conductor and earned a monthly salary of Rs.20,218/-, as evidenced by Ex.P-13.
Accordingly, the annual income of the deceased would be Rs.2,42,616/-.

It is pertinent to note that this annual income falls below the taxable slab for the financial year 2015-16,
meaning that the deceased NC: 2024:KHC-K:9520 was not liable to pay income tax during that period.
Considering the deceased's age of 37 years, as established through Ex.P-17, an additional 50% of the income must be added towards future prospects, in line with the prevailing legal principles.
6. It is important to highlight that any deduction of 10% towards income tax from the calculated compensation would be unwarranted and incorrect in this scenario.
The deceased's income of Rs.2,42,616/- per annum was below the taxable income threshold for the financial year 2015-16.
Applying a deduction for income tax when there was no actual tax liability imposes an undue financial burden on the dependents and does not align with the principles of fair compensation.
The purpose of compensation is to adequately restore the financial stability of the dependents, and unjustified tax deductions compromise this objective.
7. Since there were five dependents relying on the deceased, a deduction of 1/4th of the income is justified to NC: 2024:KHC-K:9520 account for personal expenses.
After this deduction, the effective monthly income for dependency compensation amounts to Rs.22,745.25/-.

By applying a multiplier of 15, which is appropriate for the age of the deceased, the total compensation for 'loss of dependency' is calculated as Rs.40,94,145/- (Rs.22,745.25 x 12 months x 15 years).
8.
Under conventional heads, since there are five dependents, the claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.2,30,000/-.

The accident is of the year 2016 and therefore, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1, 10%
escalation for every three years which works out to Rs.46,000/- is added under conventional heads.
The total compensation re- determined by this Court works out to Rs.43,70,145/- as against Mallappa S/O Bhimappa Shirol And Ors vs M/S Alliance Carriers And Contractors ... on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71544551/
